sourceFlowReconstruction: L1-4 Mishnah: seven days before Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol is separated from his house to the Parhedrin chamber, and another kohen is prepared in his stead lest a disqualification befall him.
L4-7 Mishnah: R. Yehuda - another wife is also prepared lest his wife die, as it says 'vekhiper ba'ado uve'ad beito', beito = his wife. They said to him: if so, there is no end to the matter.

L8-11 Gemara cites 'tenan hatam' (Parah 3:1): seven days before the burning of the parah the kohen who burns it was separated from his house to the chamber facing the Bira, north-east; it was called Lishkat Beit HaEven.
L12-14 Gemara's own question and answer (not part of the Mishnah in Parah): why was it called so? Because all ma'aseha (Rashi: of the parah) were in dung, stone and earth vessels.

L14-20 What is the reason? Since a tevul yom is fit for the parah, as we learned (detnan): they would make the kohen who burns the parah tamei and immerse him, to remove [the view] from the hearts of the Sadducees who said it was done by me'orvei shemesh; the Rabbis instituted dung, stone and earth vessels, which do not receive tumah, so that it not be treated lightly.

L20-24 Why north-east? Since it is a chatat and a chatat requires the north, and 'el nokhach penei ohel mo'ed' is written of it, the Rabbis instituted a north-east chamber so that it have a hekeira (Rashi: so he knows he was separated for the parah service, called chatat, and is zealous in its acts).

L24-27 What is Bira? Rabba bar bar Chana in the name of R. Yochanan: a place on the Temple Mount named Bira. Reish Lakish: the whole Mikdash is called Bira, as it says 'haBira asher hakhinoti'. No resolution.

L27-31 Mena hanei milei? R. Minyomi bar Chilkiya - R. Machseya bar Idi - R. Yochanan: 'ka'asher asah bayom hazeh tzivah Hashem la'asot lekhaper aleikhem' - la'asot = acts of the parah, lekhaper = acts of Yom Kippur.
L32-34 Challenge: granted the whole verse cannot be about the parah, since lekhaper is written and the parah is not for atonement; but say the whole verse is about Yom Kippur?

L34-38 Answer (amri): learn tzivah-tzivah: here 'tzivah Hashem la'asot', there 'zot chukat haTorah asher tzivah Hashem lemor'; as there parah so here parah, and as here separation so there separation.

L39 've'eima' - a further challenge begins and is cut off by the physical end of 2a. Nothing beyond the tzivah-tzivah answer is reached on this daf; that answer is itself under challenge when the daf ends.

Advisory only: 'so called because all its service used...' has an ambiguous 'its' (Rashi: ma'aseha = of the parah); consider clarifying when s02 is repaired.

perSugya.evidence: L1-4 support separation, Parhedrin, backup kohen 'shema ye'era bo pesul'. L4-7 support R. Yehuda's backup wife, the reason 'shema tamut ishto', the verse Lev 16:6 and 'beito zo ishto', and the Sages' 'im ken ein ladavar sof'. 'Replacement wife could also die' and 'tamei' are Rashi's glosses (Rashi lines 8, 11-12) and are consistent. Misconception is accurate: the Mishnah records no dispute over the derashah. finalRuling states the tanna kamma's rule and the Sages' rejection, both on L3-7; not a copy of the hint. sourceRefs l01/l04 with vilnaLine 1,4,6,7 are inside the range. Tags are slugs; requiresUnderstanding empty; hint is a question.

The citation of Parah, the seven days, the chamber facing the Bira north-east and the name Beit HaEven match L8-11. The name explanation matches L12-14 in content. Defects below concern attribution and referent.

defects.says: 'the Mishnah explains that it comes from the vessels used in all the chamber's service'
defects.sourceSupports: The Mishnah in Parah ends at 'veLishkat Beit HaEven hayetah nikret' (L11). 'Velamah nikra shemah...' (L12-14) is the Gemara's own question and answer (the module's own source layer for Yoma.2a.3 reads 'The Gemara explains: And why was it called...'; argumentFlow step-02 of this same sugya also assigns it to the Gemara). Attribution defect. In addition 'the chamber's service' misidentifies 'ma'aseha': Rashi (he lines 16-17) 'shekol ma'aseha - shel parah'.

defects.says: 'The Mishnah in Parah describes the same kind of seven-day separation ... and names his chamber for its vessels'
defects.sourceSupports: The Mishnah only gives the name; the explanation by the vessels is the Gemara's (L12-14). Same attribution defect.

defects.says: vessels used 'in its service' with 'its' = the chamber
defects.sourceSupports: Rashi: the acts are those of the parah. Lesser referent imprecision; fix together with the above so the record is consistent with step-02 ('actions associated with the heifer') and with s03.

That statement is made by the Gemara only at L18-19 ('dela likablu tumah'), which belongs to s03. Rashi's Hebrew on L12-14 does not say it. Advisory placement note: either drop the clause or mark it as explained in the next sugya.

perSugya.evidence: L14 question; L14-17 'keivan ditvul yom kasher befarah, ditnan metam'in hayu hakohen... umatbilin oto lehotzi milibban shel Tzeddukin shehayu omrim bime'orvei hashemesh hayetah na'aseit'; L18-20 'takinu lah rabbanan... dela likablu tumah ki heikhi dela lizalzelu bah'. All fields follow this order and causality; the misconception correctly separates the immersion (anti-Sadducee) from the vessels (anti-laxity). sourceRefs l14/l18 inside range. 'publicly'/'deliberately' are glosses of 'lehotzi milibban', not contradicted. finalRuling is independent of the hint.

L20-24: 'mai shena tzefonah mizrachah; keivan dechatat hi vechatat te'unah tzefonah, ukhtiv bah el nokhach penei ohel mo'ed, takinu lah rabbanan lishkah tzefonah mizrachah ki heikhi delehevei lah hekeira'. Verse quote matches Num 19:4. 'East' and the priest's vigilance come from Rashi (he lines 37-42: 'shehu bekotel mizrachi', 'veyasim lev lihyot zariz'), used as clarification.
